definition: An American option can be exercised at any time up to expiration; a European option can only be exercised at expiration.
core_idea: Although American options technically allow earlier exercise, this distinction rarely matters much for energy options on forwards/futures, since reselling an option is almost always more profitable than exercising it early.
key_points: American option: exercisable any time before expiration.
European option: exercisable only at expiration.
Because options on forwards/futures reduce the benefit of early exercise, whether an option is American or European is usually not economically significant in this market.
trading_implications: Traders generally prefer to resell an option rather than exercise it early, regardless of its style.
caveats: Assuming American-style optionality is always a major value driver — for forward/futures-based energy options it is usually immaterial.
